components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single next action on a marketing or game surface.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 48px; padding: 16px 22px; border: 0; border-radius: 12px; background: #35e0c8; color: #05070d; font: 700 12px/1 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .16em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: filter .18s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), box-shadow .18s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); box-shadow: 0 0 32px rgba(53,224,200,.24); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #f4f7ff; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.html: MOTION SYSTEMYour body is the controller.

narrative.overview: Motion looks like a game waking up in a dark room. Its existing logo is the canonical visual idea: movement is visible as a trail, and the person is the input. The world stays near-black so motion, score, and state changes can carry the light.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black fields with one luminous motion accent.
Human geometry and movement trails instead of decorative gradients.
Short, confident game language with large readable moments.
Red and yellow reserved for actual game state, never decoration.
The existing Motion logo is preserved exactly.

rules.name: The Tracking Signal Rule
rules.body: Teal identifies motion or the next action. It does not become a generic wash across every surface.

rules.name: The Across-the-Room Rule
rules.body: Important state and the primary action must remain legible at television distance.

rules.name: The Dark-Room Rule
rules.body: A surface earns elevation only when it focuses play or explanation.

dos: Do use the motion trail to explain body-as-controller.
Do keep the page predominantly Night Field and reserve teal for motion and action.
Do label simulator evidence and physical-device gaps plainly.
donts: Don't expose or link the internal web game, relay, room codes, or camera mode.
Don't add cyan-purple gradients, gaming HUD clutter, or generic esports typography.
Don't use Impact Red or Ready Yellow as decorative accents.
Don't fabricate live tracking, customers, testimonials, availability, or performance numbers.
